concepts.name: Acidity, Basicity & Aromaticity (Huckel's Rule)
concepts.summary: Hückel's Rule: Cyclic, planar, completely conjugated systems with $(4n+2)\pi$ electrons are aromatic ($2, 6, 10, 14\pi$). Basicity of amines: Aliphatic amines are more basic than aniline because aniline's lone pair is delocalized into the benzene ring by resonance.
concepts.common_traps: Cyclooctatetraene ($8\pi$) is non-planar (tub-shaped), hence it is non-aromatic, NOT anti-aromatic!
concepts.tips_and_tricks: In gas phase, amine basicity follows strictly $+I$: $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ > \text{NH}_3$.

concepts.name: Reaction Intermediates & Electronic Effects
concepts.summary: Heterolytic fission creates ions (carbocations, carbanions); homolytic fission creates neutral free radicals. Stability of carbocations: $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ > \text{CH}_3^+$ (governed by hyperconjugation and $+I$). Stability of carbanions: $\text{CH}_3^- > 1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ$.
concepts.common_traps: In homolytic cleavage, each atom takes one bonding electron; in heterolytic cleavage, the more electronegative atom takes both electrons.
concepts.tips_and_tricks: Resonance stabilization always dominates over inductive effect, EXCEPT for halogens on benzene rings where $-I$ dominates.

## 2. Comprehensive Concept Deep-Dive & Source PYQ Links

### 2.1 Acidity, Basicity & Aromaticity (Huckel's Rule) (Physical-Chemical Properties)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **5 PYQs** (Moderate Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Hückel's Rule: Cyclic, planar, completely conjugated systems with $(4n+2)\pi$ electrons are aromatic ($2, 6, 10, 14\pi$). Basicity of amines: Aliphatic amines are more basic than aniline because aniline's lone pair is delocalized into the benzene ring by resonance.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{Aromatic: } (4n+2)\pi \text{ electrons}, \quad \text{Anti-aromatic: } 4n\pi \text{ electrons}
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Cyclooctatetraene ($8\pi$) is non-planar (tub-shaped), hence it is non-aromatic, NOT anti-aromatic!

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: In gas phase, amine basicity follows strictly $+I$: $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ > \text{NH}_3$.

#### Linked Representative PYQs:
- **[2025 Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"$\text{Which of the following is not an aromatic compound}$..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2023 Shift] Q#3 (MCQ)**: *"Among the following. The set which represents aromatic species is..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2021 Shift] Q#4 (MCQ)**: *"Arrange benzene, $n$ -hexane and ethyne in decreasing order of their acidic behaviour...."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2020 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"Which of the following is the strongest base?..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

### 2.2 Reaction Intermediates & Electronic Effects (Core Principles)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **4 PYQs** (Moderate Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Heterolytic fission creates ions (carbocations, carbanions); homolytic fission creates neutral free radicals. Stability of carbocations: $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ > \text{CH}_3^+$ (governed by hyperconjugation and $+I$). Stability of carbanions: $\text{CH}_3^- > 1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ$.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{Carbocation Stability: } 3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ > \text{CH}_3^+, \quad \text{Carbanion Stability: } \text{CH}_3^- > 1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: In homolytic cleavage, each atom takes one bonding electron; in heterolytic cleavage, the more electronegative atom takes both electrons.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Resonance stabilization always dominates over inductive effect, EXCEPT for halogens on benzene rings where $-I$ dominates.

#### Linked Representative PYQs:
- **[2026 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"The intermediates in heteropolar reactions are..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring KCET Pitfalls in General Organic Chemistry

### 1. Speed & 80-Second Constraint Management
KCET demands answering 60 questions in 80 minutes (~1.33 minutes per question). The most lethal trap is spending 3+ minutes on long algebraic derivations. Always check for dimensional consistency or option substitution first.

### 2. NCERT & Karnataka PU Board Direct Lines
Over 45% of KCET theory questions are taken directly from NCERT / Karnataka PU Board textbook summary points, margins, and standard exemplar questions. Pay rigorous attention to exceptions (e.g., electron gain enthalpy of Cl vs F, acidic nature of boric acid, non-polar symmetrical geometries).

### 3. Unit Conversions & Prefix Overlooks
Units of molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), micro/nano multipliers (10^-6, 10^-9), and centimeter-to-meter conversions in optics and gravitation account for the highest frequency of careless mark losses in KCET.

### 4. No Negative Marking Advantage
Since KCET has NO negative marking, never leave any question unattempted. When down to two options, use dimensional elimination or parity checks to maximize expected score.
